title: nontrivial domain obligation
source: STAGE0.md first pass, S3; WHAT.md, Start here (the current encoding, with revision 10's additions)
statement: Evaluate the definite integral of (ln x)/x from 1 to e.

S3-ring.why: The same proof with ftc checked by ring. deriv's output and the integrand both ring-normalise to ln x * inv(x) (E3), so field is not needed, and ring owes no divisor (§6.2). This pins that ring's check emits nothing.

notes: The range [1, e_const] cannot be ordered by norm_num, so every step that uses it owes 1 <= e_const (E4), which only e_gt_one's sign fact closes (§5.3 rev 9).
ln x owes x > 0 where it enters (E26), on [1, e_const] for the integrand and for F, and d_ln owes it again on (1, e_const).

WHAT.md's 'rewrite [ln_e, ln_one]' is two steps here, because the kernel's rewrite takes one entry. Its 'close ... by norm_num' is check ring here, because close takes ring or field and norm_num runs only on obligations (E7).
